question: According to the Census of India 2011, which state of India has the highest number of Scheduled Caste population ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uttar Pradesh has the highest Scheduled Caste (SC) population in India, according to the Census of India 2011.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's SC population constitutes around 20.5% of the state's total population.
 
• The state government and central government have various schemes and policies in place to uplift the socio-economic status of the SC population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Castes (SC)**

 
 
• Scheduled Castes are groups of people who are historically marginalized and discriminated against in India.
 
• The Indian Constitution provides certain privileges and rights to SCs to help uplift their socio-economic status.
 
• They are entitled to reservations in education, jobs, and legislatures.
 
• Various government schemes aim to improve their living conditions and provide opportunities for growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Census of India**
 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial (every 10 years) exercise conducted by the Government of India to gather demographic data.
 
• It covers various aspects such as population size, density, distribution, and socio-economic characteristics.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country.
 
• The data collected helps in planning and implementing various government policies and programs.
 
 
 
• **Reservation Policy**
 
 
• The reservation policy in India provides reserved quotas for certain sections of society, including SCs, STs, and OBCs, in education, employment, and legislatures.
 
• It aims to ensure equal opportunities and representation for historically disadvantaged groups.
 
• The policy is implemented as per the guidelines provided by the Indian Constitution.
 
• Various state and central government bodies monitor and enforce these reservations.
